about.title: City of Industry Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: City of Industry is a small, largely commercial and industrial city in the San Gabriel Valley, but the people who work here, and their families who live nearby, still rely on nearby clinics, urgent care centers, and hospitals for everyday medical needs. When a provider misreads a test, rushes a diagnosis, or makes an error during a procedure, the effects can follow a patient for years. Medical malpractice claims in California are different from a typical injury case: the law (MICRA) sets strict notice and filing deadlines, requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in, and caps certain damages. A bad result by itself isn't proof of malpractice, so these cases hinge on a careful review of medical records and provider conduct. We can review your situation and explain your options. We handle these claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Speak With an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: MICRA's Notice and Filing Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to act, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider. Missing these windows can end a claim before it's reviewed.

items.title: An Expert Has to Weigh In
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone doesn't establish malpractice, California requires a qualified medical expert to evaluate whether the care fell below the accepted standard. We can help arrange that review early, while records and details are fresh.

items.title: Damage Caps That Change Each Year
items.desc: California law caps non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, and that cap rises annually. We can walk you through how the current cap applies and what it means for your specific claim.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after a procedure near City of Industry, does that mean it was malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law is clear that a poor result alone isn't enough; the care has to have fallen below the accepted medical standard. We work with a qualified medical expert to help determine whether that standard was actually breached in your case.

items.question: How much time do I have to bring a claim?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the harm and no more than three years from the date of injury, whichever comes first. There's also a required 90-day notice to the provider before a lawsuit can be filed, so it helps to talk with us sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in medical malpractice cases, though that cap increases each year under state law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are handled separately. We can explain how these categories apply to your situation.

items.question: How do you charge for your services?
items.answer: We handle medical malpractice claims on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
